what_happened: The job to raise the drain max_concurrency ceiling from 8 to 16 was rejected at the final verdict because the test check failed. The kept output for that check is only CI checkout cleanup (git config includeIf removal, orphan process cleanup) and a Node.js 20 deprecation warning. It names no test or assertion. No unmet acceptance criteria, blockers or major findings are listed. This is the third rejection of the same ceiling change, after 20261105-180339-w5h7 and 20261106-012852-h7de. Whatever test broke is unknown from the event.
cause: The check result stores the tail of the CI log, and the tail is post-job cleanup text. The failing test's output is cut off, so the record cannot be used to diagnose anything. Nothing extracts failing test names from the test runner, and the test check is judged only once, at the final verdict. The producer never gets a test failure it can act on, and the same ceiling change is rejected repeatedly with no new information.
prevention: When the test check fails, Athena should capture and store the failing test names and assertion output from the test runner itself (for example the `failures:` section of cargo test), not the tail of the CI log. If no test name can be extracted, it should mark the result "failure unreadable" instead of passing the cleanup text on. The producer should run the same test command before finishing and get that output. This would have shown which test broke on the ceiling change, such as a pinned value, an unregistered shard-timings entry or stale help text, and it applies to every rejection of this kind.
proposed_request: Raise the drain max_concurrency ceiling from 8 to 16. Before finishing, run `cargo test` from the repo root and fix any failing test. Search the whole repo, including CLI help text, docs, tests and xtask/shard-timings.txt, for the old ceiling of 8 and update every place that restates it. Acceptance: (1) the config and code accept max_concurrency up to 16 and refuse 17; (2) no file still states a ceiling of 8; (3) `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` pass. In your report, list the test names that failed on the first run and what you changed to fix each. Also change Athena so a failed test check stores the failing test names and assertion text from the test runner output instead of the CI log tail.
